Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-04 14:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Lena (VectraHealth Platform), Marco (ML Infra), Priya (Security), Omar (Product)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on environment readiness, network access, and a small triage of latency outliers seen friday. Agreed next bench run parameters and ownership for VPC peering, pricing sketch, and security questions.

Topics:
- Access and VPC peering status
- Bench results quick review and outlier analysis
- KV cache warmup strategy and batch sizing
- Security/KMS and data retention questions
- Next-run scope and milestones

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya: all right everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda, status on peering, bench followup and then security Qs. keep it short if we can.
[00:00:18] Lena: sounds good, we only have 30 minutes on our end but should be fine.
[00:00:25] Jonah: i'll start with the bench summary, we ran the sample workload thursday night against the hosted endpoint, 95th p99 looked fine but we saw intermittent 800ms spikes at token 1 for certain session shapes. suspect cold kv cache and a couple of request headers causing falls to a different execution path.
[00:00:50] Marco: yeah i pulled the logs, and for 3% of sessions the sequence length was much shorter so batching decisions kicked different codegen, that aligns with your path selection note. can you clarify how you detect compatible model variants?
[00:01:12] Jonah: sure, so runtime picks kernels based on the sequence length distribution and quant profile, if the client sends max_tokens or truncation differently sometimes it hits a slower path. we recommended consistent prompt templates and prefix caching; that resolved 70% in our lab.
[00:01:36] Priya: quick security note - before we let you into the VPC we need to confirm KMS integration approach and also retention windows. we have a strict 30-day retention policy for pilot data and require CMKs for any logs that persist.
[00:01:55] Maya: understood. we can provide our KMS integration doc and a checklist. jonah, can you capture what we need exactly for per-customer CMK and audit log flow?
[00:02:08] Jonah: yep, i'll include required IAM roles, kms key policy samples, and the expected audit log fields.
[00:02:18] Omar: timeline wise we want to validate the steady-state latency by next thursday so product can sign off for feature gating. is that feasible?
[00:02:27] Jonah: yes if we get VPC peering by tuesday and the bench run on wednesday night, we can analyze by thursday morning. the big risk is peering firewall rules; any NAT or proxy can add jitter.
[00:02:45] Lena: we can open the peering request today, but need subnet ranges and the port list.
[00:02:52] Maya: i'll add the port list to the followup. jonah, i'll also cc our infra engineer who sets up peering.
[00:03:00] Marco: on the spikes, do you recommend dedicated capacity or can we tune the hosted pool? obviously cost matters for us.
[00:03:10] Jonah: tradeoff is predictability vs unit-cost. hosted can be tuned with aggressive kv cache warmup and prefilling batch windows, but dedicated gives you absolute control over tail latency because you avoid multi-tenant interference. for a pilot i usually recommend hosted with a small dedicated reserve if peak concurrency is high.
[00:03:31] Marco: how small of a reserve? we have about 1.2k concurrent api calls during the test window, peaks to 2k.
[00:03:40] Jonah: i'd suggest a dedicated pool sized for 1.5k steady state and burst to 2.5k, or hosted with autoscale and a warmup plan if you prefer no commitment. i'll sketch both cost estimates.
[00:03:55] Priya: one more security Q: do you support customer-managed HSM for key storage or only KMS? any SOC2 evidence?
[00:04:06] Maya: we support cloud KMS integrations and offer bring-your-own-key via customer-managed CMKs; HSM-level on-prem HSM is part of our Private deployment conversation. we have SOC2 Type II reports and redacted audit artifacts we can share under an NDA.
[00:04:22] Priya: ok send that to me, i'll flag anything that needs legal review.
[00:04:28] Jonah: back to the bench, two quick mitigations we applied in Friday's run: prefix caching of the first 64 tokens and a batching threshold increase from 8 to 12. that reduced avg token time by about 12% and smoothed some spikes.
[00:04:48] Marco: nice. what about kv cache TTL, should we keep it very long? our sessions are short lived but many repeat prompts occur across users.
[00:04:57] Jonah: recommend TTL of 5-15 minutes for pilot, depending on memory footprint. we'll instrument hit rates and advise.
[00:05:05] Lena: on the network diagram, do you need our internal DNS or will we talk to an ip range?
[00:05:11] Maya: we need subnet ranges; hostnames are optional but can help with troubleshooting.
[00:05:15] Omar: if firewall rules are strict, can we fall back to a secure gateway?
[00:05:20] Jonah: yes, we have a gateway flow that proxies through an HTTPS tunnel and preserves KV semantics, slightly higher latency but works as a fallback.
[00:05:29] Priya: can you summarize what we should expect latency-wise with the gateway?
[00:05:33] Jonah: add ~30-50ms tail for the proxy hop, plus whatever your NAT introduces. it's usually acceptable for non-realtime flows.
[00:05:42] Maya: okay let's list the blockers: VPC peering, firewall ports, KMS questions, and the bench run to repro the spikes.
[00:05:51] Lena: we'll start the peering request after this call and aim to share ranges by tomorrow.
[00:05:56] Maya: great. Jonah, do you want to run through the exact bench spec we need?
[00:06:00] Jonah: yes. plan: simulate 2k concurrent sessions with real prompt mix, include 15% short-session shapes to trigger the slow path, KV warmup of first 500 common prefixes, run for 30 minutes, collect p50/p95/p99 and token-level traces for the spikes. mesh the logs to S3 bucket shared with us.
[00:06:25] Marco: do you need any special headers or auth tokens to reproduce the same execution path?
[00:06:29] Jonah: include consistent max_tokens header and content-type application/json; avoid chunked transfer encoding. and if possible include a seed user-id header so routing keeps session affinity.
[00:06:41] Omar: sounds doable.
[00:06:43] Priya: regarding audit logs, what format do you export and how long will they exist on your side?
[00:06:50] Maya: audit logs can be exported to your S3, we recommend retention of 30 days for pilot but can be customized. logs are pushed encrypted using the customer's CMK if provided.
[00:07:02] Priya: perfect. i'll prepare a few questions about redaction and minimal fields.
[00:07:06] Jonah: last operational note: if you expect bursty traffic, enable our prefix cache and set batch windows to 30ms for interactive flows; for batch flows you can raise batch windows and reduce unit cost.
[00:07:20] Marco: ok we'll try prefix cache and the 30ms as a baseline.
[00:07:25] Maya: quick recap and owners: jonah runs bench (due 5/7), maya shares port list and pricing sketch (due 5/8), lena shares peering ranges (due 5/6), priya sends security questions (due 5/10).
[00:07:42] Omar: also please include a short doc on rollback playbook, just in case we need to flip to fallback model or degrade gracefully during spikes.
[00:07:50] Jonah: yes i'll draft a 1-page fallback playbook and include model variant fallback steps.
[00:07:56] Maya: cool. any other blockers?
[00:08:00] Lena: none from infra beyond the peering request.
[00:08:04] Priya: none right now.
[00:08:06] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and the bench template.
[00:08:12] Omar: appreciated.
